source.title: Anxious individuals have difficulty learning the causal statistics of aversive environments

confidence_rationale: This is the closest thing in the literature to a direct test of ARC-052's clause (2) IN THE AVERSIVE DOMAIN, and it carries a pupillometric index of noradrenergic gain that speaks to the neuromodulatory clause as well. Held at 0.72 rather than higher because n=31 with the key individual-difference correlations at r=-0.42 (p=0.02) and r=-0.51 (p=0.005) is a modest evidential base for the moderation result, and because pupil diameter is an indirect proxy for locus coeruleus activity, which the authors themselves flag.
failure_signatures: Volatility-driven precision adjustment is not a fixed property of the architecture but an individual-difference variable: high trait anxiety was associated with a reduced change in learning rate between stable and volatile blocks (r(28)=-0.42, p=0.02), i.e. a system can have the volatility machinery and still fail to use it.

The pupil (noradrenergic) response to volatility was itself blunted in high-anxiety individuals (r(26)=-0.51, p=0.005), so a neuromodulatory precision gain can decouple from the volatility signal it is supposed to transmit -- a wiring in which 5-HT/NE multiplicatively scales precision inherits this as a failure mode, not merely as a tuning knob.

The authors could not establish that the deficit is specific to aversive learning: a reward version showed no anxiety effect, but the task-by-anxiety difference was not itself statistically significant, so harm-specific precision control is suggested rather than shown.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In a two-armed bandit where choices could deliver electric shock, low-trait-anxious participants raised their learning rate in a volatile block relative to a stable block while high-trait-anxious participants did not; pupil dilation tracked volatility at the group level (F(1,26)=9.8, p=0.004) and the volatility-related pupil response was reduced in high-anxiety individuals, which the authors interpret as possibly reflecting altered noradrenergic responsivity.
mapping.ree_translation: Direct support for ARC-052 clause (2) in the harm domain specifically: the weight given to an accumulated aversive estimate is modulated by inferred volatility of the threat environment. The pupillometry additionally supports the neuromodulatory half of the claim -- that precision GAINS are set by an ascending modulator rather than being intrinsic to the encoder -- and identifies norepinephrine as the modulator carrying the volatility term. In REE terms: z_harm_a precision falls under threat volatility, and the fall is implemented by a gain signal external to the harm encoder, which is what ARC-052 proposes to wire in V4 via the neuromodulatory modules.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The manipulated quantity is the volatility of shock PROBABILITY given a cue, not the stability of an accumulated homeostatic deviation; SD-011's z_harm_a is the latter. The noradrenergic interpretation rests on pupil diameter as an LC proxy, which the authors explicitly say they cannot confirm without pharmacological manipulation. Trait anxiety is a between-subject moderator, so the causal direction (blunted NE gain causes poor volatility adaptation, or vice versa, or a common cause) is not identified. Finally, this study speaks only to z_harm_a; it says nothing about clause (1), the forward-model-accuracy dependence of z_harm_s precision.
mapping.source_context: 31 healthy adults (22 female, 18-40, mean 23.7) screened across the trait-anxiety range; two 90-trial blocks (stable 75/25, volatile reversing every 20 trials at 80/20); trial-varying shock magnitude; concurrent pupillometry.

confidence_components.notes: Mapping fidelity is the highest in this pull because the domain is aversive and the neuromodulatory index is measured rather than assumed. Source quality is discounted for n=31 and for individual-difference correlations in the r=0.4-0.5 range, which is the effect-size band where replication is not guaranteed.
